title: Messaging and Presence are the service; XMPP is a provider
summary: Applications consume semantic Messaging and Presence objects. XMPP representation and wire protocol remain provider-private.
invariants: Public objects include Message, MessagingAddress, PresenceState and subscription/provider abstractions; JIDs and XML stanzas do not leak into application semantics.
Full ooRexx objects remain intact through dispatch; transport convenience must not flatten them into dictionaries or strings.
Provider discovery is capability-based and dynamic rather than hardwired to XMPP.
MUC/chat rooms, PubSub, file transfer, avatars and federation-policy frameworks are outside core Messaging/Presence.
Optional extensions register their own semantic service/provider surface and cannot silently grow the core Messaging contract.

provenance.claim: Defines semantic Messaging/Presence objects and provider access classes.
